method.value: Exponentially tapered power law I(R)=A(R/Rc)^-g1 exp[-(R/Rc)^g2], Fourier transformed with Galario, compared to visibilities with MCMC

evidence.quote: The parameters are explored with 100 walkers and 5000 steps

fitting.value: emcee MCMC; medians with 16th-84th percentiles scaled by sqrt(reduced chi2)

evidence.quote: The quoted uncertainties are the interval from the 16th to the 84th percentile of the model chains and scaled by the square root of the reduced $\chi^2$ of the fit.

findings_qualitative.value: All disks with R_eff,95% ≥55 au show substructures; compact smooth disks resemble inner cores of ring disks.

evidence.quote: In contrast, all disks with $R_{\rm eff,95\%}$ of at least 55 au in our sample show detectable substructures.

claims.hypothesis: Do smooth and substructured disks differ in stellar or disk properties?
claims.experiment: KS tests of stellar mass, age and luminosity across subsamples
claims.result: Mass, age and luminosity are similar to smooth disks in singles; radii differ
claims.finding: Dust disk size is the main distinguishing property

evidence.quote: However, the disks with subtructures have preferentially larger radii in mm-size grains.

claims.hypothesis: Inner cores of ring disks resemble compact smooth disks
claims.experiment: Compare Rc, gamma1, gamma2 and peak brightness
claims.result: Parameters fall within smooth disk ranges

evidence.quote: The inner emission cores of the extended ring disks have comparable radius, peak brightness, power law index ($\gamma_1$), and taper index ($\gamma_2$) to the compact smooth disks.

claims.hypothesis: Size-luminosity relation holds and indicates optically thick compact disks
claims.experiment: Linmix regression of R_eff,95% vs L_mm

evidence.quote: Some of the compact disks may be optically thick, while extended disks contain some regions that are optically thin
